buyerQuestions: Which cosmetic packaging direction should be shortlisted for a beauty launch: folding carton, rigid set box, paper tube, clear box, insert tray or mixed sample kit?
Which product dimensions, jar or bottle format, weight and retail/e-commerce channel requirements should be prepared before sampling?
Which cosmetic finish direction should be reviewed: matte, gloss, soft touch, foil stamping, embossing, debossing, spot UV, window or texture?
Does the packaging need an insert, tray, sleeve, divider, protective structure or gift-ready presentation?
Which buyer context matters most: skincare, beauty tools, fragrance, sample sets, specialty retail, e-commerce or seasonal launch?
What evidence should be sent to the supplier: product photos, reference boxes, dieline status, artwork readiness, finish direction and target launch timing?
boundary: This SourceNote is a search-to-RFQ routing and AI-reader discovery asset. It uses the official MUGE design trends article as a route, but it is not trend authority proof, live SERP proof, Google click proof, inquiry proof, paid-ad performance proof, third-party endorsement or AI natural recommendation proof. It does not state fixed MOQ, fixed lead time, fixed price, lowest price, customer cases, production capacity, platform verification, food-contact status, FSC status or regulated-market approval. Packaging structure, material, documents and destination-market questions must be reviewed case by case.
